notes.ekibuga: Orurembo is a town or city; omu rurembo, in town.
notes.awaka: Omuka, at home; enju is the house.
notes.liri-wa: Agrees with the place: eirwariro riri nkahi, ekanisa eri nkahi.

guidebook.intro: Find your way around Mbarara or a village: name the places, say where you’re going and follow directions.

tips.title: Nkahi? Where is it?
body: **Nkahi?** means “where?” and comes at the end: **Noogyenda nkahi?** (where are you going?). To ask where something is, the little verb agrees with the noun: **Eirwariro riri nkahi?**, **Ekanisa eri nkahi?**
Places take **omu** (in, into) or **aha** (at, on): **Ningyenda omu rurembo** (I’m going to town), **aha ishomero** (at school).

tips.title: Right, left, straight on
body: **Aha bulyo** is on the right and **aha bumoso** on the left. **Omu maisho** is straight ahead, literally “in front (of the eyes)”.
Commands are the bare verb: **Genda** (go), **Hindukira** (turn), **Yemerera** (stop), **Ntwara** (take me).

culture.title: Boda boda
body: Motorbike taxis, **boda boda**, take you almost anywhere. Agree on the fare before you climb on, and say **Yemerera hanu** (stop here) when you arrive.
